item.title: CineSense 2.165.0
item.description:
CineSense 2.165.0

  • Settings → Editors: color videos by camera or by frame rate; put every slow-motion video on its own track; make one timeline per frame rate (each at its own native rate — 23.976, 59.94, 119.88…) or one per camera.
  • Settings → Cards & Drives: give a card its own Resolve track (beside its color).
  • Custom Send… (finished screen, menu, or "Customize before sending" in Send a Folder…): every option for this one send, which project to send to, and Save as preset. Send to Resolve can follow a preset.
  • A video you removed from a timeline stays off it when new footage is added. Building a new timeline asks whether to leave those videos out; a timeline you emptied completely starts fresh with every video.
  • A video deleted from the media pool comes back on the next send — never onto a timeline it was removed from.
  • Sending is much faster: video descriptions are worked out for the day being sent only (Settings → Editors → "Add video descriptions"), and each video's details are kept between sends.
  • New installs: each camera on its own track, colored by camera ("Cameras: Own tracks / One track"). Your own settings stay as they were.
  • Custom Send: remembers how a day was last sent (preset included), warns when the footage is vertical, explains each timeline choice, and the clock icon marks slow motion. "By camera" is gone — one timeline per camera covers it.
  • Presets can be made in Settings → Editors (New preset…).
  • A folder holding several shoot days asks to send them as separate days, each in its own bin under the folder's name.
  • Custom Send's Tracks grid shows where each camera will land and follows Own tracks / One track as you click.
  • Timelines CineSense builds have no empty tracks it added, start at 01:00:00:00 (Stacked: the time of day), and name tracks after the camera.
  • Cameras set to different time zones: the finish says so, Chronological orders by each video's exact clock, and Stacked can show its ruler in the zone you choose ("Ruler time").
  • Fixes: frame-rate flag colors follow your Settings; flags off takes CineSense's own flags off; no empty timeline when nothing is placed; "Keep the real pauses" starts off; a one-frame rounding no longer spills a video to a second track.
  • Fix: renaming a card keeps its Resolve color and track.

item.title: CineSense 2.164.0
item.description:
CineSense 2.164.0

  • Press Send to Resolve with Resolve closed: CineSense opens it, asks which project (or makes a new one with the shoot's name), and sends. DaVinci Resolve Studio only; Settings → Editors → "Open DaVinci Resolve when I send".
  • Frame-rate flags: videos sent to Resolve are flagged by the rate they were filmed at, and a Rose marker shows a rate that clashes with the timeline (Settings → Editors).
  • CineSearch: overnight jobs ask first only when they're long (you choose how long), and its Python can be copied into CineSense's own folder.
  • Smaller: "Card cleared" wraps its sentence and names at most two folders, a clear reads "cleared 50" in Recent, and Settings describes the new Resolve behaviour.

#### Frame-rate flags on Send to Resolve (built 2026-10-14)

In plain words: Settings → Editors has a new switch, "Flag videos by frame rate" (off until you turn it on). With it on, every video a send hands Resolve gets a flag in the media pool for the rate its camera filmed at — Sky under 40 fps, Lemon 40–80, Cocoa 80–150, Fuchsia 150 and over, Cream when the file cannot be read — and you can pick each group's colour from Resolve's own sixteen flag colours. Camera colours stay exactly as they were. CineSense only ever adds or clears its own flag, so yours stay, and a flag you take off stays off. A video whose rate does not fit the timeline (25 fps on a 23.976 timeline, 30 on 29.97) gets a Rose marker. (Built on 2.163.2, whose fix for a Stacked send of a captioned drone day it carries.)

##### Measured first (Resolve Studio 21.1.0.14, a throwaway project)

  • A flag is the MEDIA POOL clip's: it shows on the clip's items on every timeline (video and audio), a timeline item's AddFlag/ClearFlags act on the clip, and appended and rippled items carry it. AddFlag takes the sixteen FlagColor names in any case, once; a clip colour's name, "All" and "" are refused. GetFlagList adds a `__flags` number key. A timeline item's marker is the item's own. His project was saved first, the throwaway deleted, and his project reopened on its timeline and page. How a flag LOOKS on a busy timeline was not captured (Resolve's window was on another Space). All of it is in CLAUDE.md, "A flag lives on the media".
  • The flag swatches are read out of Resolve's binary (`Flag<Name>`, agreeing with `ClipFlag<Name>Small` and `ClipMarkerIndicator<Name>` for all sixteen): `tools/resolve_clip_palette.py` reads flags too, and its `--check` (the board's "resolve: palette" row, now 32 rows) holds `ResolveFlagColor` in Engine.swift to them.

##### The engine (cinesense.sh)

  • `--rate-flags` and `--rate-flag-colors c1,…,c5`: five flag colours, no two the same, canonical spelling — else bryzr's picks, said in the log.
  • `rate_group` (one awk function): the rate FILMED at (slow_decide's TF — a DJI saved slowed is its 120; a variable-rate phone its average, F-5) into under 40 / 40–80 / 80–150 / 150 and over / not measured. Flags on, a send measures every video (once, kept in slow-facts.tsv). No ffprobe at all: nothing is flagged, and the send says why.
  • The Lua (FLAGS block, lifted by the suite): the clip's flag set in the harvest, whatever the layout; recorded on the clip (`cinesense_rateflag`: "Sky" added, "=Sky" the editor's already there); a recorded flag gone from the clip stays gone; a colour change moves ours by its own colour; never ClearFlags("All").
  • The Rose pass (RATEFIT block, lifted): each video THIS send placed whose rate as Resolve plays it (clip rate × speed) is not the same kind (exact or 1000/1001) and family (24/30 or 25) as the timeline's — a timeline marker "25 fps on a 23.976 fps timeline"; never a video CineSense slowed, never a variable-rate one.
  • The legend: one line in the CineSense layout marker of a timeline built with the flags on (words only — not a layout key, so switching the flags on asks nothing). The answer: `rate_flags` (added this send, by group, with their range), `rate_misfit`, `rate_off`, `rate_refused`, `rate_skipped`, and one log line.
  • The send's Lua keeps 2.163.2's fix: the flags add ONE top-level name (`RF`, a table that holds the rest), and the busiest stacked send — now with the flags on — keeps room for nine more.

##### The app

  • Settings → Editors → "Flag videos by frame rate": the switch, and with it on the five groups, each with a picker of Resolve's sixteen flag colours drawn from the measured values; a colour another group has is shown and refused, naming that group ("Each group needs its own color.").
  • `ShippedDefault.rateFlags` (false) and `rateFlagColors` (Sky, Lemon, Cocoa, Fuchsia, Cream); stored colours a send would refuse read as those.
  • The finished panel: "Frame-rate flags: 41 at 24–30 · 12 at 50–60 · 3 at 120", "2 at 25 fps don't fit the 23.976 fps timeline (Rose markers)", a flag you took off "left off", and several days added up.
  • `CINESENSE_SNAP_ONLY=rate-flags --snap-ui <dir>`: the row off, on, with custom colours, narrow and wide.

##### Checks

  • test-resolve-send (+33 rows): every group boundary both sides (39.9/40, 79.9/80, 149.9/150), the DJI saved slowed, 959.04, the varying phone, the unread file; custom colours, refused colours, off by default; the rate rule run on 23 pairs; whole sends against the stand-in (flags modelled from the measurement — a flag is the clip's): flags set, no bystander touched, Rose markers on 25/30/100 and never on 29.97, the varying phone or a slowed video, stacked too; a re-send keeping the editor's own flag and leaving off the one they took off, Rose never twice; a colour change; the editor's flag of our colour kept as theirs; the app's JSON and the log. 2.163.2's busiest-send rows now send with the flags on.
  • Controls (copies of the suite against mutated engines): re-flagging what the editor un-flagged reddens 3 rows; ClearFlags("All") reddens 1; dropping the harvest's do-block reddens the busiest-stacked row ("room for only 1", with the flags on); dropping both slowed-video guards reddens 1 — dropping only the speed check stays GREEN, because the rate it really plays at holds alone (said in the engine comment and CLAUDE.md).
  • `--selftest-2164` (35 rows, in the whole self-test): the sixteen flag names in the API's order, every one with a measured swatch (a grey one refused), the picker's refusal and its words, the shipped defaults against a scratch suite, what a send carries, and the finished lines for one day and several.

#### CineSearch: its own Python, and small overnight catch-ups run without asking (built 2026-10-14)

In plain words: CineSearch ran on the Python inside the developer folder (`~/Projects/sd-ingest`), so moving or deleting that folder would have switched CineSearch and the overnight pass off. It can now have its own copy, in CineSense's folder: one button in Settings → Advanced copies it (no download, almost no disk), checks it works, and only then uses it — the original is kept, and it can be put back. And the overnight pass now asks for your OK only before a job over an hour (your choice: 30 min, 1 h or 2 h), so the half-hour sharper-search catch-up runs by itself tonight.

*CineSearch — its own Python (bryzr's go, 2026-10-14):*

  • One answer to "which Python" — `VisionPython` (VisionPython.swift): the store's venv (`Application Support/CineSense/vision/venv`, one spelling; Python's `paths.venv_dir()`) first; the checkout's only when the store has none that works, or when a DEBUG build is asked for it (`CINESENSE_VISION_PYTHON=checkout`, ignored by a release build). A copy still being moved (`.cinesense-unproven`) is never chosen; a `bin/python` whose interpreter is gone reads as broken, not as there. `choose` is pure; every caller still asks `VisionTool.python`, and `VisionTool.installed` asks the same choice. The launch logs which one and why.
  • The move — `vision/venv_home.py move | rollback | status` (stdlib only, bundled): proves the source first; APFS-clones it (7.9 s for the owner's 1.1 GB, measured into a scratch store) or copies it keeping every timestamp; rewrites the text files that name the old folder (MEASURED: only `bin/*` and `pyvenv.cfg` do — a `.pyc`'s path is fixed by importlib at load); refuses if a BINARY names it; builds under `.venv-moving.<pid>`, renames into place carrying the unproven mark, then proves it where it lives — its prefix is the new folder, numpy/PIL/pyarrow/lancedb/torch/ open_clip/transformers all load FROM the copy and never from the original, no `bin/` script still starts the old Python, `bin/pip` answers for the copy — and only then drops the mark and writes `.cinesense-venv.json`. A copy that fails is taken back; the source is only ever read. `rollback` takes back only a copy a move made, and only while its source still works. A killed run's hidden folder goes by exact name once its pid is gone.
  • Settings → Advanced → CineSearch's Python says which Python and why, with the path, and — while it is the developer folder's and the store has none — "Copy and check…" (a confirm; about a minute). The move's own object is observed, never AppModel.
  • The overnight job names its interpreter: launch reconciles a job that names another Python ("repointed"), and a finished move repoints it at once (installed app only, as every write of the real job).

*Small catch-ups run without asking (bryzr's call):*

  • "Ask before overnight jobs longer than [30 min / 1 h / 2 h]", Settings → CineSearch → Overnight pass, default 1 h (`ShippedDefault. nightAskOverMinutes`, pinned in the self-test). The app writes it to `vision/preferences.json` as `ask_over_minutes`; `paths.big_job_minutes()` reads it every time it is asked (the gate, the daemon's notice), the suites' `CINEVISION_BIG_JOB_MINUTES` still wins. Absent: the hour. A value Settings never offers, or a file that cannot be read: the strictest line (30), never a longer one. Run It Now, Approve For Tonight and one ping per waiting job are unchanged.
  • The waiting PE-Core fill (~31 min) runs by itself the next night.

*Tests:* `vision/test_venv_home.py` (19 rows, in test_vision.py; its CONTROL breaks the rewrite and the proof must refuse the copy), the gate on both sides of each line in test_vision.py (179 / 181 new videos around the hour, 181 / 361 around 2 h, the PE-Core fill, bad values), test_night_audit's real-gate fixture over the new hour (200 videos); `--selftest-2164-cinesearch` (40 rows: which Python in every case, venv states from scratch folders, the offer, the answer, the repoint, the setting) and in the whole self-test.

#### Merged onto 2.163.5 (2026-10-17)

Both branches were cut before 2.163.3–2.163.5 and merged onto 2.163.5's last commit (e96e9031) on `feature/2164-rebased`. What the merge itself changed:

  • The engine's `resolve_sent` event carries 2.163.4's `stack_held` (T155) and the rate fields; the stand-in harness prints both kinds of line.
  • The finished screen's "Frame-rate flags:" line sets its counts apart with `NumberFacts.gap`, never " · " (2.163.5's rule).
  • The nightly job is rewritten for a missing `ExitTimeOut` (2.163.3) before it is repointed at the chosen Python; the CineSearch self-test's "as bryzr's Mac wrote it" job now carries the key, so it reads "repointed".
  • test_vision.py: the new gate rows keep the notification stand-in (T115 puts the real send back after the last gate), and the notify-isolation and venv-home tests both run.
  • test_notify_isolation.py (T115): its real-gate fixture is 181 new videos (60.3 min), over the shipped hour; the afternoon's 91 (30.3 min) now runs on its own and pings nothing, so the row could not have seen a send.

item.title: CineSense 2.163.5
item.description:
CineSense 2.163.5

  • When the files on a card are already in the folder (say, after reinstalling), the copy panel now counts steadily up to the end and says "Checking copies already there…" — it no longer flickers between 0 and 1.
  • The finished screen holds still: "Ejecting the card…" is there from the start, and the slow-motion check is one short line that doesn't change the panel's size.
  • A drive that is too full says "Not enough room on <drive>" at the bottom of the panel, and the space it shows is the space that really counts (macOS's "free" includes space it only clears later).
  • In an account that can't change the main Applications folder, CineSense offers to move itself into your own Applications folder instead, and never touches another account's copy.
  • Numbers sit apart: sizes, counts and times are spaced instead of joined by "·", and a count beside a date gets its own small badge.
  • Records: a record in "Needs a look" can be dismissed once you've dealt with it (and brought back); it keeps its red or orange mark in the full list and its log is never changed.
  • The card panel's footer and Preview button no longer shift while it checks, the panel no longer jumps for a frame when it reopens, and CineTransfer's Start never freezes the window while it asks the drives.
  • The steady count also holds for a card that starts by itself before its check is back (auto-ingest, a queue), and CineSync, Settings and CloudSense's test lines keep their numbers apart too.
  • CineTransfer and CloudSense: a service dragged to Destinations shows straight away; Start never does nothing in silence — it starts, or says why; the upload bar never slides backwards; and CloudSense's lists and Records keep their columns apart at any window size (less important columns step aside, the record panel sits beside the list or over it).
  • Settings → Cards: one failed check no longer tells you to retire a card ("often the drive or cable, not the card", with Clear); a pulled drive's run never counts against the card.
  • Records: "Dismiss all" at the top of Needs a look, Dismiss beside Export for one record; the record panel fits its width when you drag the divider; a photos-only "nothing new" record says "16 photos already there".
  • Records: the column headings line up with their columns when scroll bars are always shown, and a day's dash box takes that day's ticks off instead of ticking the rest.
  • The finished screen's CineSearch box keeps one height, and a drive's name never wraps beside its badge.
  • Smaller things: "1 file" and "3 files" instead of "file(s)", an ejected drive in Settings → Advanced is shown by its own name, sizes everywhere read like "2.0 GB", a record of an ingest that copied nothing says "Nothing new — already copied", and a sentence that was cut in the middle now wraps.

item.title: CineSense 2.163.4
item.description:
CineSense 2.163.4

  • Pull a drive out in the middle of a copy and CineSense stops within about a second and says so, plainly: what was copied and checked, what wasn't, and what happened on the card. Nothing you haven't got a checked copy of is ever removed from a card.
  • A Resolve timeline you rename is treated as your edit: later videos go on at its end, and any that were filmed in the middle wait in the day's bin instead of being squeezed in.
  • The card panel says what each drive really needs for this copy, shows "N copied" the moment a card goes in (green once it's proven), and never cuts a drive's name.
  • Records has a calmer list: tick boxes appear when you hover, problem rows have a red or orange edge, numbers line up under their headings, and the footer tells you if something you ticked is scrolled out of view.
  • Reports: clearer names, one kind per report, and you can delete them. A finished copy or ingest now shows a Mac notification as well as the phone ping.
  • Smaller things: one size for a folder everywhere, every linked cloud account offered, a new glass meter for drive space, the CineTransfer window stays in front when you click it, and a slower, smoother light round the search box.

item.title: CineSense 2.140.0
item.description:
CineSense 2.140.0

  • Every Dropbox and Google Drive sign-in asks the service who it is (Dropbox's account id and email, Drive's permissionId and email) and keeps it with the account. The card names it: `you@example.com · CineSense`.
  • Sign in again to a different account is never silent. A dialog names both — "This is a different Dropbox account (new@…) from the one Dropbox was linked to (old@…)" — with Cancel (blue: nothing changes; sign out of Dropbox in the browser first, then Sign in again) or **Use as a New Account** (the old account is unlinked — its History stays, nothing on either account is touched — and the new one is linked and tested).
  • An account linked before 2.140.0 learns who it is the first time Settings → CloudSense is opened (its own token, refreshed with its own client), and its next Sign in again compares with that. **bryzr's Dropbox will read brian@bryzrstudio.com** — the account it is really linked to now; signing in again with the 5.5 TB account asks first.
  • If the service cannot be asked (offline), the sign-in goes through as before, is said as "could not ask which account", and nothing recorded is erased; 2.138.1's size check still speaks after the test.

item.title: CineSense 2.129.2
item.description:
CineSense 2.129.2

  • A linked Dropbox, Google Drive, Backblaze B2 or Amazon S3 account now receives its sign-in or keys. Until this version none of them could connect, whatever you did; a Storage Box was never affected. If you linked one already, press Test again — there is nothing to re-link.

item.title: CineSense 2.129.1
item.description:
CineSense 2.129.1

  • Opening CineSense from Downloads no longer adds a login item for a copy macOS deletes on restart. It starts at login once it is in your Applications folder — and if you choose "Not Now" on the move offer, it now says so.
  • Click the CineSense icon in the menu bar for its menu; right-click it for the ingest panel (it was the other way round). The panel still appears by itself when a card goes in, and stays in the menu as Ingest Panel.
  • CloudSense's panel: two clear icons switch between the big card and the compact list, a bigger gear opens its settings, and "Stay awake" (a moon and a switch) sits alone at the bottom. Clicking the upload line in the menu always opens the big card.
  • A single large video uploads over one connection to a Storage Box or SFTP server, so a day of one big file goes slower than a day of many. The panel now says so when it happens, and Test connection shows that one-connection speed and what a single 100 GB file would take.
  • Copy Diagnostics reports memory the way About This Mac does (a 64 GB Mac says 64 GB).

item.title: CineSense 2.129.0
item.description:
CineSense 2.129.0

  • CineSense is now signed by Bryzr Studio and notarised by Apple: open it and macOS asks only the usual "downloaded from the internet — Open?". No Terminal commands, no System Settings detour.
  • Opened from Downloads, CineSense offers to move itself into Applications, where it starts at login and updates install.
  • Updates come by themselves: CineSense checks once a day, and a new version is a line at the top of its menu — nothing pops up. An update never installs while a card, a transfer or an upload is in progress; it waits, then CineSense relaunches by itself. Settings → About → Check for Updates checks now, and "Receive beta updates" offers test versions first.
  • Something went wrong? Menu → Copy Diagnostics shows exactly what it will gather, can hide your card and folder names, and puts it all in a folder in Downloads for you to email to beta@bryzrstudio.com. CineSense never sends anything itself, and never includes footage, passwords or keys.
